title: Aesthetics, Axes, and Scales
text: toy dataset pairs two incompatible measurements genomic positions: z-scored signal centered around zero, read-depth count 50–200 range. Plotting single y-scale crush one , natural fit secondary axis. %+% operator returns seq_plot invisibly, render plot assign expression p reference last line chunk — knitr auto-prints result via print.SeqPlot(), calls $plot() current device.
code: win <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 1e6)) d <- GRanges("chr1",              IRanges(seq(2e4, 1e6, by = 2e4), width = 1),              score = rnorm(50),              depth = round(rpois(50, 100) +                            40 * sin(seq(0, pi, length.out = 50))))

title: Aesthetics, Axes, and Scales
text: axis namespace four levels specificity: SeqPlotR resolves key, walks specific general: axis.x1.line.col -> axis.x.line.col -> axis.line.col -> built-default. first match wins.
code: p <- seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(data = d, windows = win,             aesthetics = aes(               axis.line.col    = "grey50",   # all axes               axis.y.line.lwd  = 1.5,        # both y axes               axis.x1.line.col = "firebrick" # primary x overrides             )) %+%   seq_point(map(x = start, y = score),             aesthetics = aes(color = "steelblue")) p

title: Aesthetics, Axes, and Scales
text: keys can written nested form. aes(axis.x = aes(position = "top")) identical aes(axis.x.position = "top"), components can grouped topic rather spelled one one.

what: Scale expansion, breaks, caps, and limits
title: Aesthetics, Axes, and Scales
text: axis’s scale options live axis.<side>.scale.*: scale.expand = c(mul, add) — proportional (mul times data range) absolute padding around data. Default c(0.025, 0). scale.breaks — explicit break positions. Otherwise n_breaks picks pretty() breaks. scale.minor_breaks — scalar (number sub-divisions) explicit vector. "capped" (default) runs first last break. "full" spans expanded plot range. "exact" spans unexpanded data range. "ticks" suppresses axis line shows tick marks.  Equivalent prefer explicit scale object: Expansion applies element coordinates well axis. Points outside (expanded) range handled oob: "exclude" (default) drops reports count, "perimeter" clamps limit. pretty = list(...) forwards extra arguments base pretty() break placement.
code: p <- seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(data = d, windows = win,             aesthetics = aes(               axis.y1.scale.limits        = c(-3, 3),               axis.y1.scale.breaks        = c(-2, 0, 2),               axis.y1.scale.cap           = "capped",               axis.y1.scale.minor_breaks  = 3             )) %+%   seq_point(map(x = start, y = score)) p seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(data = d, windows = win,             scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(               limits       = c(-3, 3),               breaks       = c(-2, 0, 2),               minor_breaks = 3,               cap          = "capped"             )) %+%   seq_point(map(x = start, y = score)) gx <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(sample(1:1e6, 200), width = 1),               xv = runif(200, -3, 13), score = runif(200, 0, 6)) mk <- function(lab, ...) {   seq_track(data = gx, windows = win, mapping = map(x = xv, y = score),             scale_x = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 10), ...),             aesthetics = aes("axis.x.title.label" = lab)) %+% seq_point() }  (seq_plot() %+%    mk("expand = c(0.2, 0)", expand = c(0.2, 0)) %__%    mk("oob = exclude", oob = "exclude") %__%    mk("oob = perimeter", oob = "perimeter") %__%    mk("pretty = list(n = 10, min.n = 5)", pretty = list(n = 10, min.n = 5)))$plot() #> 22 out-of-bounds data points excluded! (seq_point) #> 72 out-of-bounds data points excluded! (seq_point) #> 72 out-of-bounds data points plotted! (seq_point) #> 72 out-of-bounds data points excluded! (seq_point)

title: Aesthetics, Axes, and Scales
text: element opts secondary axis adding axis.x = 2 axis.y = 2 map(). SeqPlotR infers independent scale elements, draws second axis, positions element new scale. default positions x1 = bottom, x2 = top, y1 = left, y2 = right.  Moving axis unusual position just matter setting position. axes side stack automatically, lower-indexed axis (x1, y1) sitting closer panel.
code: p <- seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(data = d, windows = win,             aesthetics = aes(               axis.y1.line.col = "firebrick",               axis.y2.line.col = "steelblue"             )) %+%   seq_point(map(x = start, y = score),             aesthetics = aes(color = "firebrick")) %+%   seq_line(map(x = start, y = depth, axis.y = 2),            aesthetics = aes(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1.2)) p #> 50 out-of-bounds data points excluded! (seq_line) p <- seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(data = d, windows = win,             aesthetics = aes(               axis.x1.position = "top",               axis.x2.position = "top",               axis.x1.line.col = "firebrick",               axis.x2.line.col = "steelblue"             ),             scale_x2 = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 1))) %+%   seq_point(map(x = start, y = score)) p

what: Axis titles, blanked chrome, and in-panel axes
title: Aesthetics, Axes, and Scales
text: default axis title comes first element’s mapping, track mapping, seqname genomic axes (last track shows default, xv). Override axis.<side>.title.label styled aes(label, col, size). Setting structural sub-key (line, title, ticks, labels, text, gridline) NA blanks , like element_blank().  Titles range labels can also live inside panel axis.<dim>.title.position axis.<dim>.labels.style / .position. y title sits NPC (0.02, 0.95) single bracketed range label replaces per-tick labels.
code: gt <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(start(d), width = 1),               xv = runif(50, 0, 10), score = d$score)  (seq_plot() %+%    (seq_track(data = gt, windows = win, mapping = map(x = xv, y = score),               aesthetics = aes(axis.x.title = aes(label = "Styled title",                                                   col = "#A0282C", size = 1))) %+%       seq_point()) %__%    (seq_track(data = gt, windows = win, mapping = map(x = xv, y = score),               aesthetics = aes("axis.x.line" = NA, "axis.x.ticks" = NA,                                "axis.x.text" = NA)) %+%       seq_point()))$plot() win <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 1000)) gr  <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(100, 400, 700), width = 80),                score = c(1, 3, 2))  p <- seq_plot() %+%   (seq_track(      data    = gr, windows = win,      aesthetics = aes(        "axis.y.title.text"      = "Score",        "axis.y.title.position"  = c(0.02, 0.95),        "axis.y.labels.style"    = "range",        "axis.y.labels.position" = c(0.02, 0.05)      )    ) %+%    seq_bar(map(x = start, y = score))) p$plot()

title: Aesthetics, Axes, and Scales
text: track.* namespace controls rectangle shared windows; track.window.* controls per-window panel rectangle. inherit — ’re semantically distinct.
code: p <- seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(data = d, windows = win,             aesthetics = aes(               track.background.fill        = "#faf8f5",               track.border.col             = "grey30",               track.window.background.fill = "white",               track.window.border.col      = "grey60"             )) %+%   seq_point(map(x = start, y = score)) p

title: Aesthetics, Axes, and Scales
text: Gridlines drawn positions axis ticks, default. Enable per dimension axis.x.gridline = TRUE axis.y.gridline = TRUE aes() either seq_plot() seq_track(). follow dotted-path hierarchy every axis key — axis.gridline.* sets base defaults, axis.x.gridline.* / axis.y.gridline.* override per dimension.  can also pass aes() directly value. Supplying styling sub-keys enough enable gridline; separate = TRUE needed:  axes can shown together. shared base style comes axis.gridline.*, per-dimension keys override :  Gridlines respect standard plot-level vs track-level theme precedence. plot-level axis.y.gridline = TRUE suppressed track B via track-level override:
code: p <- seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(data = d, windows = win,             aesthetics = aes(               axis.y.gridline       = TRUE,               axis.y.gridline.color = "grey80",               axis.y.gridline.lwd   = 0.5             )) %+%   seq_point(map(x = start, y = score)) p p <- seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(data = d, windows = win,             aesthetics = aes(               axis.y.gridline = aes(color = "grey80", lwd = 0.5)             )) %+%   seq_point(map(x = start, y = score)) p p <- seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(data = d, windows = win,             aesthetics = aes(               axis.y.gridline       = TRUE,               axis.x.gridline       = TRUE,               axis.gridline.color   = "grey85",               axis.gridline.lwd     = 0.4,               axis.x.gridline.lty   = 2   # dashed x only             )) %+%   seq_point(map(x = start, y = score)) p win2 <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(1, 1e6 + 1), c(1e6, 2e6)))  p <- seq_plot(aesthetics = aes(axis.y.gridline       = TRUE,                                axis.gridline.color   = "grey85")) %+%   seq_track(track_id = "A", data = d, windows = win2) %+%   seq_point(map(x = start, y = score)) %__%   seq_track(track_id = "B", data = d, windows = win2,             aesthetics = aes(axis.y.gridline = FALSE)) %+%   seq_line(map(x = start, y = depth), aesthetics = aes(color = "steelblue")) p

title: Aesthetics, Axes, and Scales
text: Themes set seq_plot() apply every track; themes seq_track() override track . precedence ggplot2’s theme() plus per-facet overrides.
code: win2 <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(1, 1e6 + 1), c(1e6, 2e6)))  p <- seq_plot(aesthetics = aes(     axis.line.col    = "grey30",     axis.text.size   = 0.55,     track.border.col = "grey70"   )) %+%   seq_track(track_id = "A", data = d, windows = win2) %+%   seq_point(map(x = start, y = score)) %__%   seq_track(track_id = "B", data = d, windows = win2,             aesthetics = aes(axis.y1.line.col = "firebrick")) %+%   seq_line(map(x = start, y = depth), aesthetics = aes(color = "firebrick")) p

title: Aesthetics, Axes, and Scales
text: axis component: axis[.side].{line,ticks,text,title}.{col,lwd,size,angle,visible}. scale option: axis[.side].scale.{limits,breaks,minor_breaks,expand,cap,n_breaks}. Track position: axis.<side>.position = "top"|"bottom"|"left"|"right". Route element secondary axis: map(axis.x = 2) map(axis.y = 2). Flat nested forms equivalent: aes(axis.x.line.col = "red") == aes(axis.x = aes(line = aes(col = "red"))). Track chrome: track.{background,border}.{fill,col,lwd,alpha} track.window.{background,border}.{fill,col,lwd,alpha}. Gridlines: axis.x.gridline = TRUE / axis.y.gridline = TRUE enable; style via axis.[x|y].gridline.{color, lwd, lty, alpha} inheriting axis.gridline.*. Passing aes(color, lwd, ...) value also enables.

title: Rearrangements: Blocks, Connectors, and Derivative Chromosomes
text: seq_block() draws one box per range. data GRanges whose seqnames window block sits . map() supplies reference interval block shows (chrom, ref_start, ref_end), label, flipped flag fill key. default fill solid colour per key, tinted tint.  fill = "cytoband" reference interval filled cytoband pattern (bundled hg38 bands unless cytobands given). Flipped blocks mirrored, centromere interval drawn bowtie.
code: blk <- GRanges("der1", IRanges(c(1, 3e7, 6e7), c(3e7, 6e7, 1.2e8)),                label = c("A", "B", "C"), flipped = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE),                tint = 1:3, ref_start = c(0, 3e7, 6e7), ref_end = c(3e7, 6e7, 1.2e8),                cs = c(NA, NA, 9e7), ce = c(NA, NA, 9.5e7)) bm <- map(label = label, flipped = flipped, tint = tint, chrom = "chr1",           ref_start = ref_start, ref_end = ref_end,           centromere_start = cs, centromere_end = ce)  print(seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(windows = GRanges("der1", IRanges(1, 1.2e8)), aesthetics = aes(axis.x.visible = FALSE)) %+%   seq_block(blk, bm)) print(seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(windows = GRanges("der1", IRanges(1, 1.2e8)), aesthetics = aes(axis.x.visible = FALSE)) %+%   seq_block(blk, bm, fill = "cytoband"))

title: Rearrangements: Blocks, Connectors, and Derivative Chromosomes
text: label_inside map() places label inside block fits. flip_style marks flipped blocks rotating label, drawing overline, adding minus sign.
code: blk$label_inside <- TRUE bm2 <- map(label = label, flipped = flipped, tint = tint, chrom = "chr1",            ref_start = ref_start, ref_end = ref_end, label_inside = label_inside) p <- seq_plot() for (st in c("rotate", "overline", "minus")) {   p <- p %+% seq_track(track_id = st, direction = "under",                        windows = GRanges("der1", IRanges(1, 1.2e8)),                        aesthetics = aes(axis.x.visible = FALSE)) %+%     seq_block(blk, bm2, flip_style = st) %+%     seq_track_label(st) } p

title: Rearrangements: Blocks, Connectors, and Derivative Chromosomes
text: annotations takes data frame chrom, start label; row drawn every block whose reference interval contains , mapped flips. strand adds direction arrow.  Arrow blocks (shape = "arrow") point toward increasing reference coordinate reverse flipped.
code: ann <- data.frame(chrom = "chr1", start = c(1.5e7, 4.5e7), end = c(NA, 5.5e7),                   label = c("geneX", "geneY"), strand = c("+", "-")) print(seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(windows = GRanges("der1", IRanges(1, 1.2e8)), aesthetics = aes(axis.x.visible = FALSE)) %+%   seq_block(blk, bm, annotations = ann)) print(seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(windows = GRanges("der1", IRanges(1, 1.2e8)), aesthetics = aes(axis.x.visible = FALSE)) %+%   seq_block(blk, bm, shape = "arrow"))

title: Rearrangements: Blocks, Connectors, and Derivative Chromosomes
text: Rows different lengths line track sets x_span = "shared". Every window placed coordinates union span, base pairs per unit width equal every row, gaps windows follow coordinates.
code: ref <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 1.2e8), label = "chr1", ref_start = 0, ref_end = 1.2e8) der <- GRanges("der1", IRanges(c(1, 3e7), c(2.5e7, 1e8)), label = c("A", "B"),                ref_start = c(0, 3e7), ref_end = c(2.5e7, 1e8)) mp <- map(label = label, chrom = "chr1", ref_start = ref_start, ref_end = ref_end) margins <- list(top = 0, bottom = 0, left = 0.13, right = 0.02) tk <- function(id, w) seq_track(track_id = id, direction = "under", windows = w, x_span = "shared",                                 track_outer_margin = margins, track_inner_margin = 0,                                 window_outer_margin = 0, window_inner_margin = 0,                                 aesthetics = aes(axis.x.visible = FALSE)) p <- seq_plot(plot_margin = 0.02) %+%   tk("ref", GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 1.2e8))) %+% seq_block(ref, mp) %+% seq_track_label("chr1") %+%   tk("der", GRanges("der1", IRanges(c(1, 3e7), c(2.5e7, 1e8)))) %+% seq_block(der, mp) %+%   seq_track_label("der(1)", sublabel = "toy") p

title: Rearrangements: Blocks, Connectors, and Derivative Chromosomes
text: seq_connector() joins block edges: within row draws stemmed bulge, across rows curve facing edges. side0/side1 choose left right edge, style picks line style. Defaults exist junction, inferred unused. seq_synteny() accepts twisted (swaps target corners inversions), smooth (smoothstep sides) layer = "" (drawn blocks). seq_caption() adds text plot, optional banner.
code: cn <- data.frame(chrom0 = "der1", x0 = c(1, 1), x0_end = c(2.5e7, 2.5e7), side0 = c("right", "left"),                  chrom1 = "der1", x1 = c(3e7, 3e7), x1_end = c(1e8, 1e8), side1 = c("left", "right"),                  kind = c("junction", "unused"), bulge = TRUE) syn <- data.frame(chrom0 = "chr1", chrom1 = "der1", x0 = c(1, 3e7), x0_end = c(2.5e7, 1e8),                   x1 = c(1, 3e7), x1_end = c(2.5e7, 1e8), fill = c("#4E79A7", "#F28E2B"),                   twisted = c(FALSE, TRUE)) print(p %+%   seq_synteny(syn, map(x0 = x0, x0_end = x0_end, x1 = x1, x1_end = x1_end, chrom0 = chrom0,                        chrom1 = chrom1, fill = fill, twisted = twisted),               t0 = "ref", t1 = "der", height = 0.5, smooth = TRUE, layer = "below",               aesthetics = aes(alpha = 0.6, color = NA)) %+%   seq_connector(cn, map(x0 = x0, x0_end = x0_end, chrom0 = chrom0, side0 = side0, x1 = x1,                         x1_end = x1_end, chrom1 = chrom1, side1 = side1, style = kind, bulge = bulge),                 t0 = "der", t1 = "der", show_legend = FALSE) %+%   seq_caption("Toy example", banner = "APPROXIMATE"))

title: Rearrangements: Blocks, Connectors, and Derivative Chromosomes
text: seq_read_table_set() reads versioned set tables directory <prefix>.<table>.tsv files, list data frames carrying schema_version. Cells typed columns.tsv manifest, unsupported versions missing columns stop message naming set. package ships reconstructions table sets extdata/rose/derivatives.
code: root <- system.file("extdata", "rose", "derivatives", package = "SeqPlotR") head(list.files(root), 4) #> [1] "bfb_c1_block"     "bfb_c1_block_ref" "bfb_c1_walk"      "bfb_c2_block" s <- seq_read_table_set(file.path(root, "inv_block"), "plot_derivatives") names(s) #> [1] "rows"       "blocks"     "connectors" "ribbons"    "windows"    #> [6] "caption" s$rows[, c("row_id", "kind", "label")] #>   row_id       kind  label #> 1      1  reference   chr1 #> 2      2 derivative der(1)

title: Rearrangements: Blocks, Connectors, and Derivative Chromosomes
text: seq_rose_derivatives() turns plot_derivatives table set (produced ROSE package) plot, one track per row, junction connectors, optional ribbons caption. maps table columns onto elements , result ordinary SeqPlot.  synteny = TRUE adds ribbons reference derivative row. Twisted ribbons show inverted segments. Window gaps follow coordinates reference layout.  Walk fixtures include loose derivative rows. show_loose = FALSE drops together rows continue .   Cluster fixtures add copy number tracks rows draw candidate strips arrows.  Solid fills use default palette, palette = "soft", vector named block key. block_colors overrides label, label_inside = TRUE puts labels inside blocks wide enough.  result SeqPlot, elements can added %+%.
code: seq_rose_derivatives(file.path(root, "inv_block"))$plot() seq_rose_derivatives(file.path(root, "chromoplexy_block_ref"), synteny = TRUE)$plot() walk <- file.path(root, "bfb_c1_walk") seq_rose_derivatives(walk)$plot() seq_rose_derivatives(walk, show_loose = FALSE)$plot() seq_rose_derivatives(file.path(root, "ct18_cluster"),                      synteny = TRUE)$plot() seq_rose_derivatives(file.path(root, "inv_block"), fill = "solid",                      palette = "soft", label_inside = TRUE, flip_style = "minus")$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Every primitive shares three-stage contract (initialize → prep → draw) shorthand: seq_<name>(map(...), aesthetics = aes(...)). differs map() vocabulary one consumes. Per-track data + mapping inherited, single seq_track() can host several primitives drawing table.

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Required map() fields: x, y. Optional: color, fill, size, shape, alpha. , SNV simulated BFB amplicon chr2 point position, VAF y, coloured true number mutated copies (mult). SNVs inside amplified region carry several copies.
code: seq_plot(aesthetics = aes(margins = list(top = 0, right = 0.12,                                          bottom = 0, left = 0))) %|%   seq_track(data = bfb_snv,             mapping = map(x = start, y = vaf),             windows = bfb_win) %+%   seq_point(map(color = mult),             aesthetics = aes(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.8)) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Required: x, y. aes(type = "step") switches step line (useful signal tracks represent piecewise-constant values). , simulated BFB amplicon chr2 shown mean SNV VAF 1 Mb bins (smooth) piecewise-constant copy number segment (step). rise across amplified region.
code: bfb_win_snv <- subsetByOverlaps(bfb_snv, bfb_win) bin_start   <- seq(start(bfb_win), end(bfb_win) - 1e6, by = 1e6) bin_id      <- factor(findInterval(start(bfb_win_snv), bin_start), seq_along(bin_start)) bfb_bins    <- GRanges("chr2", IRanges(bin_start + 5e5, width = 1),                        mean_vaf = as.vector(tapply(bfb_win_snv$vaf, bin_id, mean)),                        n_snv    = as.vector(table(bin_id))) seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(track_id = "Mean VAF",             data = bfb_bins,             mapping = map(x = start, y = mean_vaf),             windows = bfb_win) %+%   seq_line(aesthetics = aes(color = "#205EA6", linewidth = 1.4)) %__%   seq_track(track_id = "Copy number",             data = bfb_seg,             mapping = map(x = start, y = cn),             windows = bfb_win) %+%   seq_line(aesthetics = aes(color = "#AF3029",                             linewidth = 1.4,                             type = "step")) -> p p$plot() #> 1 out-of-bounds data points excluded! (seq_line)

what: seq_segment — one straight line per row
title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Required: x, x_end, y, y_end. Great quick interval marks — peak span, read pair, Manhattan-style baseline. , copy-number segment simulated chromothripsis event chr3 horizontal line total copy number; oscillation CN 3 CN 1 chromothripsis signature.
code: seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = ct_seg,             mapping = map(x = start, x_end = end,                           y = cn, y_end = cn),             windows = ct_win) %+%   seq_segment(aesthetics = aes(linewidth = 3, color = "#205EA6")) -> p p$plot()

what: seq_curve — Bezier curve with data-space control points
title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Required: x, y, x_end, y_end. aes(curvature) sets fractional y-offset control points (default 0.3). Handy visualising directional relationships (transcript splice, read pair) without stealing arch slot (seq_arc) used SV calls.
code: curve_gr <- GRanges("chr1",   IRanges(start = c(1.2e6, 1.7e6, 2.3e6), width = 1),   x_end = c(1.5e6, 2.1e6, 2.7e6),   y     = c(0.2,   0.3,   0.25),   y_end = c(0.5,   0.7,   0.6))  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = curve_gr,             mapping = map(x = start, x_end = x_end,                           y = y, y_end = y_end),             windows = win) %+%   seq_curve(aesthetics = aes(curvature = 0.5,                              color = "#66800B",                              linewidth = 1.4)) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Required: x, y. Optional group splits path several disconnected lines. Good plotting per-group traces one track.
code: group_xs <- seq(1.05e6, 2.95e6, length.out = 30) path_gr  <- GRanges("chr1",   IRanges(start = rep(group_xs, 3), width = 1),   y     = c(sin((group_xs - 1e6) / 5e5) * 0.2 + 0.4,             cos((group_xs - 1e6) / 4e5) * 0.2 + 0.5,                  ((group_xs - 1e6) / 2e6) * 0.3 + 0.3),   trace = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 30))  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = path_gr,             mapping = map(x = start, y = y,                           group = trace, color = trace),             windows = win) %+%   seq_path(aesthetics = aes(linewidth = 1.3, alpha = 0.85)) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Required: x, y. Optional group partitions vertices across multiple polygons. Use custom region highlights hand-shaped overlays. : three filled triangles, one per gene body.
code: tri_starts <- c(1.20e6, 1.80e6, 2.40e6) tri_widths <- c(2.5e5,  3.0e5,  2.0e5)  poly_gr <- GRanges("chr1",   IRanges(start = rep(tri_starts, each = 3), width = 1),   x_v = c(rbind(tri_starts,                 tri_starts + tri_widths / 2,                 tri_starts + tri_widths)),   y_v = rep(c(0.2, 0.8, 0.2), times = 3),   grp = rep(paste0("tri", 1:3), each = 3))  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = poly_gr,             mapping = map(x = x_v, y = y_v,                           group = grp, fill = grp),             windows = win) %+%   seq_poly(aesthetics = aes(color = "white", alpha = 0.8)) -> p p$plot()

what: seq_area — filled area under a curve
title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Required: x, y. Optional aes(baseline = ...) sets closing y-value (default 0). Coverage curves, pileups, smoothed density fills. , number SNVs per 1 Mb bin simulated BFB amplicon chr2; mutation counts climb copy number.
code: seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = bfb_bins,             mapping = map(x = start, y = n_snv),             windows = bfb_win) %+%   seq_area(aesthetics = aes(fill = "#4385BE",                             color = "#205EA6",                             alpha = 0.65,                             linewidth = 0.8)) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Required: x, y, label. Optional: size, color, angle, hjust, vjust.
code: text_gr <- GRanges("chr1",   IRanges(start = c(1.30e6, 1.90e6, 2.50e6), width = 1),   y_pos = c(0.75, 0.45, 0.85),   lbl   = c("peak_1", "peak_2", "peak_3"))  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = text_gr,             mapping = map(x = start, y = y_pos, label = lbl),             windows = win) %+%   seq_text(aesthetics = aes(fontsize = 12,                             color = "#AF3029",                             hjust = 0.5)) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Composites chain primitives (often plus small amount pre-computation) provide higher-level idioms. composite inherits underlying primitive exposes narrower, task-specific map() vocabulary.

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: One rectangle per observation; group stacks bars identical x positions. , segment simulated chromothripsis BFB event chr4 bar spanning segment, height equal copy number.
code: seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = ctb_seg,             mapping = map(x = start, y = cn),             windows = ctb_win,             scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 6))) %+%   seq_bar(aesthetics = aes(fill = "#4385BE")) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Supplying group mapping causes bars identical x positions stack. Colors drawn Flexoki palette keyed group level.
code: stack_gr <- GRanges(   "chr1",   IRanges(start = rep(seq(1.2e6, 2.8e6, by = 2e5), each = 3), width = 5e4),   value    = runif(27, 0.1, 0.5),   category = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), times = 9) )  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = stack_gr,             mapping = map(x = start, y = value, group = category),             windows = win) %+%   seq_bar() -> p p$plot() #> 8 out-of-bounds data points excluded! (seq_bar)

what: seq_ribbon — band between two y series
title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Required: y_min, y_max. Confidence bands, min/max pileups, CI envelopes — anything needs shaded interval per x. , band minor major allele copy number simulated chr4 event; band collapses zero width balanced segments sits major allele minor allele lost.
code: # one point at each segment edge so the band is piecewise constant ctb_edges <- GRanges("chr4",   IRanges(c(start(ctb_seg), end(ctb_seg)), width = 1),   cn_minor = rep(ctb_seg$cn_minor, 2),   cn_major = rep(ctb_seg$cn_major, 2)) ctb_edges <- sort(ctb_edges)  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = ctb_edges,             mapping = map(x = start, y_min = cn_minor, y_max = cn_major),             windows = ctb_win,             scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 3))) %+%   seq_ribbon(aesthetics = aes(fill = "#4385BE", alpha = 0.5)) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Calls stats::density() resolved y renders result filled area. Pre-computed densities use seq_area() directly. , VAF SNVs simulated whole-genome-doubling tumour chr1-3. density runs along x-axis (VAF, 0 1) bw sets bandwidth; modes come SNVs carried one, two four copies.
code: seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = wgd_snv,             mapping = map(x = start, y = vaf),             windows = GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 248956422)),             scale_x = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)),             scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)),             aesthetics = aes("axis.y1.visible" = FALSE,                                 "axis.x1.title.text" = "VAF")) %+%   seq_density(aesthetics = aes(fill = "#879A39", alpha = 0.7, bw = 0.02)) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Flat mode: one rectangle per observation, one tile per segment simulated chr4 event, shaded B-allele frequency (baf; 0.5 balanced, 1 LOH). Rotated mode (aes(rotate = TRUE)) turns tile diamond, standard Hi-C representation combined genomic y-axis (see ).
code: baf_ramp <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("#DAD8CE", "#205EA6"))(100) ctb_seg$baf_col <- baf_ramp[round((ctb_seg$baf - 0.5) / 0.5 * 99) + 1]  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = ctb_seg,             mapping = map(x = start, fill = baf_col),             windows = ctb_win) %+%   seq_tile() -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Rotated tiles (aes(rotate = TRUE)) place observation diamond (genomic_x, genomic_y) space — natural representation Hi-C contacts 2D genomic relationship. axes genomic; pass seq_scale_genomic() scale_y built distance-bin GRanges.
code: n_contacts <- 60 hic_win <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1e6, 3e6))  # Toy Hi-C: pick x-bins, then y-bins offset by a genomic distance. x_starts <- sample(seq(1.05e6, 2.95e6, by = 2e4), n_contacts, replace = TRUE) y_offset <- sample(seq(2e4, 8e5, by = 2e4), n_contacts, replace = TRUE)  x_gr <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(start = x_starts,            width = 2e4),                 score = runif(n_contacts)) y_gr <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(start = x_starts + y_offset, width = 2e4))  # Map [0,1] scores → a soft red ramp for the fill column. score_to_color <- function(s) {   pal <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("#F4A4C2", "#A02C6D"))(100)   pal[pmin(pmax(round(s * 99) + 1, 1), 100)] } x_gr$fill_col <- score_to_color(x_gr$score)  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = x_gr,             mapping = map(x = start, fill = fill_col),             windows = hic_win,             scale_y = seq_scale_genomic(               GRanges("chr1", IRanges(0, max(y_offset) + 2e4)))) %+%   seq_tile(data2 = y_gr, aesthetics = aes(rotate = TRUE)) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Vertical stem baseline (default 0) y, point y. Standard sparse discrete events (mutation impact, peak summits). , junctions simulated chr4 event, placed first breakpoint height equal junction copy number (jcn).
code: seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = ctb_sv,             mapping = map(x = start, y = jcn),             windows = ctb_win,             scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 5.5))) %+%   seq_lollipop(aesthetics = aes(color = "#AF3029", linewidth = 1.2)) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Every column reference comes map(): group joins features one gene, strand orients arrows, type distinguishes exons UTRs, label places gene name, color tints gene.
code: # reused by the gene examples below gm <- map(group = gene_id, type = feature, strand = strand_col,           label = gene_name, color = color)  gene_gr <- GRanges("chr1",   IRanges(     start = c(1.10e6, 1.20e6, 1.35e6, 1.50e6, 1.58e6,               1.90e6, 2.05e6, 2.18e6, 2.30e6,               2.55e6, 2.68e6, 2.80e6),     width = c( 3e4,  6e4,  4e4,  5e4,  2e4,                4e4,  8e4,  5e4,  3e4,                6e4,  3e4,  5e4)   ),   gene_id    = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), times = c(5, 4, 3)),   gene_name  = rep(c("TP53", "MYC", "BRCA1"), times = c(5, 4, 3)),   strand_col = rep(c("+", "-", "+"),       times = c(5, 4, 3)),   feature = c("UTR","exon","exon","exon","UTR",               "UTR","exon","exon","UTR",               "exon","exon","exon"),   color = c(rep("#205EA6", 5),             rep("#AF3029", 4),             rep("#66800B", 3)))  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = gene_gr,             mapping = gm,             windows = win) %+%   seq_gene(gm) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: backbone_type controls gene backbone rendering. "arrow" (default) places chevron arrows show strand direction. "solid" draws plain line; "dashed" uses dashed line — useful predicted low-confidence models.
code: seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = gene_gr,             mapping = gm,             windows = win) %+%   seq_gene(gm,            backbone_type = "dashed") -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: show_start = TRUE draws flag arrow first exon (row order) gene. genes annotated first exon differs true TSS, pass tss_position = list(gene_id = c(start, end)) override auto-detected position per gene.
code: seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = gene_gr,             mapping = gm,             windows = win) %+%   seq_gene(gm,            show_start = TRUE) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: separate_strands = TRUE partitions track interior two horizontal sub-bands: "+" strand genes top "-" strand genes bottom. dashed line marks band boundary band labelled. Silently ignored one strand present.
code: seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = gene_gr,             mapping = gm,             windows = win) %+%   seq_gene(gm,            separate_strands = TRUE) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: separate_strands, show_start, backbone_type independent compose freely. solid backbone — useful track already conveys directionality strand band layout.
code: seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = gene_gr,             mapping = gm,             windows = win,             track_height = 1.2) %+%   seq_gene(gm,            backbone_type    = "solid",            show_start       = TRUE,            separate_strands = TRUE) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: style_type selects per-gene rendering style. "exon" (default) full backbone-plus-exon-boxes view shown ; "gene" collapses gene single chevron-shaped polygon spanning gene extent — useful exon detail needed screen space tight; "point" reduces gene single filled circle TSS, ideal dense overviews. Labels drawn three modes.
code: seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = gene_gr,             mapping = gm,             windows = win) %+%   seq_gene(gm,            style_type = "gene") -> p p$plot() seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = gene_gr,             mapping = gm,             windows = win) %+%   seq_gene(gm,            style_type = "point") -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: aes(gene.label = aes(position = c(<"start"|"end">, <"top"|"bottom">))) composes label placement independently x y.
code: gr_genes <- GRanges("chr1",   IRanges(start = c(100,  400, 1000, 1500),           end   = c(300,  600, 1200, 1700)),   gene_id    = c("geneA", "geneA", "geneB", "geneB"),   gene_name  = c("GeneA", "GeneA", "GeneB", "GeneB"),   strand_col = c("+", "+", "-", "-"),   feat_type  = c("exon", "exon", "exon", "exon") )  win_g <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 2000))  p <- seq_plot() %+%   (seq_track(data = gr_genes, windows = win_g) %+%    seq_gene(      map(group = gene_id, label = gene_name,          strand = strand_col, type = feat_type),      aesthetics = aes(        gene.label = aes(position = c("start", "top"),                         color    = "navy",                         size     = 0.55)      )    )) p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: genes overlap, seq_gene stacks non-overlapping tiers automatically. separate_strands = TRUE strand band tier stack, keeping two strands visually separated even high gene density.
code: set.seed(7) n_genes  <- 14 starts   <- sort(sample(seq(1.05e6, 2.6e6, by = 5e4), n_genes)) widths   <- sample(seq(5e4, 3e5, by = 2e4), n_genes, replace = TRUE) strands  <- sample(c("+", "-"), n_genes, replace = TRUE) colors_d <- ifelse(strands == "+", "#205EA6", "#AF3029") gids_d   <- paste0("G", seq_len(n_genes))  dense_gr <- GRanges("chr1",   IRanges(start = starts, width = widths),   gene_id    = gids_d,   gene_name  = gids_d,   strand_col = strands,   feature    = "exon",   color      = colors_d)  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = dense_gr,             mapping = gm,             windows = win,             track_height = 1.4) %+%   seq_gene(gm,            separate_strands = TRUE) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: seq_sequence() renders coloured rectangle nucleotide windows 200 bp wide. Wider windows emit message render nothing. Colours follow UCSC standard default: green, T red, C blue, G orange/gold. rectangle drawn 99 % slot width thin gap separates adjacent bases. Supply nucleotides via sequence (character string) fetched automatically BSgenome package via genome. Set show_letters = TRUE overlay base letter windows ≤ 80 bp.
code: seq50  <- paste(rep(c("A","T","C","G","G","A","C","T","T","A"), 5), collapse = "") win50  <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 50))  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(windows = win50, track_height = 0.7) %+%   seq_sequence(sequence = seq50, show_letters = TRUE) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: window 80 200 bp letters suppressed (show_letters silently ignored) coloured blocks still render. gives compact composition pattern view without clutter overlapping labels.
code: seq100 <- paste(rep(c("A","T","C","G"), 25), collapse = "") win100 <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 100))  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(windows = win100, track_height = 0.7) %+%   seq_sequence(sequence = seq100) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: Pass named character vector colors override UCSC defaults. , soft pastel palette used make track less visually dominant layered elements.
code: pastel <- c(A = "#A8D8A8", T = "#F4A7A7", C = "#A7C4F4", G = "#FAD9A1",             N = "#DDDDDD")  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(windows = win50, track_height = 0.7) %+%   seq_sequence(sequence = seq50, show_letters = TRUE, colors = pastel) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: rect_height reserves fraction track height rectangles — useful placing seq_sequence signal track. sequence track gets short track_height allocation coverage area dominates.
code: win60  <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 60)) seq60  <- paste(rep(c("A","C","G","T"), 15), collapse = "")  cov_xs60 <- seq(1, 60, length.out = 60) cov_gr60 <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(start = cov_xs60, width = 1),                     depth = 0.4 + 0.4 * sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 60)))  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(windows = win60, track_height = 0.55) %+%     seq_sequence(sequence = seq60,                  show_letters = TRUE,                  rect_height  = 0.7) %__%   seq_track(data = cov_gr60,             mapping = map(x = start, y = depth),             windows = win60) %+%     seq_area(aesthetics = aes(fill = "#4385BE",                               color = "#205EA6",                               alpha = 0.65,                               linewidth = 0.8)) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: seq_ideogram() consumes GRanges cytogenetic bands gieStain mcol draws band Giemsa-shaded rectangle. Paired acen bands collapse two red triangles meeting centromere. Load bundled hg38 cytoband table [load_cytobands()].

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: create_genome_windows("chr1") expands GRanges spanning full chromosome, ideogram fills panel end--end.
code: cb <- load_cytobands()  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(track_id = "chr1",             windows = create_genome_windows("chr1")) %+%   seq_ideogram(data = cb) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: windows GRanges multiple ranges lays chromosome panel inside track. handful chromosomes stacked side--side gives --glance karyotype.
code: karyo_win <- create_genome_windows(c("chr1", "chr4", "chr7",                                      "chr14", "chrX"))  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(track_id = "Karyotype",             windows = karyo_win) %+%   seq_ideogram(data = cb) -> p p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: scope = "full" renders whole chromosome overlays translucent box marking highlight_range. style = "rounded" adds rounded telomere caps; telomere.radius = 1 gives full half-circle.
code: cb <- load_cytobands() chr1_full <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 248956422)) zoom_in   <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1.2e8, 1.6e8))  p <- seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(windows = zoom_in, height = 1.5) %+%    seq_ideogram(cb,                 scope           = "full",                 style           = "rounded",                 highlight_range = zoom_in,                 aesthetics = aes(                   highlight       = aes(fill = "red", alpha = 0.5),                   telomere.radius = 1                 )) p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: seq_scalebar() draws horizontal length reference panel position, useful x-axis hidden. label auto-formats length (1e5 "100 kb", 2e6 "2 Mb", 500 "500 bp"); override label = "...".
code: win_sb <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 1e6))  p <- seq_plot() %+%   (seq_track(      windows    = win_sb,      aesthetics = aes("axis.x1.visible" = FALSE)) %+%    seq_scalebar(length_bp = 1e5,                 hjust     = 0.95,                 vjust     = 0.5,                 bar_lwd   = 1.5)) p$plot()

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: default every seq_track runs genomic x along width lets elements choose y-axis scale data. Pass scale_y = seq_scale_genomic(...) flip track genomic position runs along y instead; set scale_x = seq_scale_continuous(...) (seq_scale_discrete(...)) carry scalar / categorical value x-axis. data can rendered either way. seq_track() exposes three arguments drive : scale_x — controls x-axis scale (defaults genomic range track’s windows). scale_y — controls y-axis scale. seq_scale_genomic(...) auto-enables uses_genomic_y. y_windows — shorthand set genomic y-range without constructing scale object.

title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: small gene-level table (log2fc per gene, one point per gene): Genomic x, scalar y (conventional). x = start runs along 1–3 Mb genomic window; y = log2fc scalar.  Scalar x, genomic y (flipped). scale_x carries log2fc [-3, 3]; scale_y = seq_scale_genomic(win) puts genomic position vertical axis. lollipops now fan horizontally x = 0, one row per gene true genomic coordinate.  two plots encode table — orientation genomic axis changes. flipped version y-tick labels fall back Mb units (genomic yScaleFactor, matching x-axis default) 1.5 Mb reads 1.5 rather 1,500,000.
code: gene_meta <- GRanges("chr1",   IRanges(start = seq(1.1e6, 2.9e6, length.out = 14), width = 1e4),   log2fc = c(-2.4, -1.3, 0.9, 2.1,  1.6, -0.5,  2.7,               0.4, -1.8,  1.2, 0.2,  0.8, -2.2,  1.1),   sig    = c("down","down","ns","up","up","ns","up",              "ns","down","up","ns","ns","down","up"))  sig_cols <- c(up = "#AF3029", down = "#205EA6", ns = "#878580") seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = gene_meta,             mapping = map(x = start, y = log2fc, color = sig),             windows = win) %+%   seq_segment(mapping = map(x = start, x_end = start,                             y = 0, y_end = log2fc, color = sig),               aesthetics = aes(linewidth = 2)) %+%   seq_point(aesthetics = aes(size = 0.9)) -> p p$plot() #> 14 out-of-bounds data points excluded! (seq_point) seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = gene_meta,             mapping = map(x = log2fc, y = mid, color = sig),             windows = win,             scale_x = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(-3, 3)),             scale_y = seq_scale_genomic(win),             track_width = 0.6) %+%   seq_segment(mapping = map(x = 0, x_end = log2fc,                             y = mid, y_end = mid, color = sig),               aesthetics = aes(linewidth = 2)) %+%   seq_point(aesthetics = aes(size = 0.9)) -> p p$plot()

what: Coverage signal flipped onto the y-axis
title: Elements: Primitives, Composites, and Ideograms
text: principle extends continuous signal. , coverage curve shown first conventional orientation, flipped depth runs along x genomic position along y — useful narrow sidebar next wider browser panel.
code: cov_xs <- seq(1.05e6, 2.95e6, length.out = 200) cov_gr <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(cov_xs, width = 1),                   depth = 0.5 + 0.3 * sin((cov_xs - 1e6) / 3e5)) seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = cov_gr,             mapping = map(x = start, y = depth),             windows = win) %+%   seq_area(aesthetics = aes(fill = "#4385BE",                             color = "#205EA6",                             alpha = 0.6, linewidth = 0.7)) -> p p$plot() seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(data = cov_gr,             mapping = map(x = depth, y = start),             windows = win) %+%   seq_area(aesthetics = aes(fill = "#4385BE",                             color = "#205EA6",                             alpha = 0.6, linewidth = 0.7)) -> p p$plot()

title: Genomic Data: Wrappers, Hi-C, and File Connections
text: Single-sample CN scatter coloured integer state, optional segmentation overlay. cn_col falls back c("cn", "copy_number", "CN", "state", "integer_cn") ratio_col c("log2ratio", "logR", "log2R", "ratio", "log2_ratio"). example simulated tumour chromothripsis breakage-fusion-bridge amplification chr4. simulation provides copy-number segments read-level ratios, points 100 kb bins across chr4:55-125 Mb. bin takes copy number segment containing log2 ratio log2(cn / 2), ratio expected copy number diploid reference, copy number 2 sits 0 copy number 1 -1. segment overlay uses ratio computed per segment.
code: sg  <- segs$ct_bfb win_cn <- GRanges("chr4", IRanges(5.5e7, 1.25e8))  # 100 kb bins labelled by the overlapping segment bin_start <- seq(5.5e7, 1.25e8 - 1e5, by = 1e5) bins <- GRanges("chr4", IRanges(bin_start, width = 1e5)) seg_gr <- GRanges(sg$chrom, IRanges(sg$start, sg$end), cn = sg$cn,                   seg_mean = log2(sg$cn / 2)) hit <- findOverlaps(bins, seg_gr, select = "first") bins$cn        <- seg_gr$cn[hit] bins$log2ratio <- log2(bins$cn / 2)  p <- seq_copynumber(bins, windows = win_cn,                     segment_data = seg_gr, segment_col = "seg_mean") p$plot() #> 5 out-of-bounds data points excluded! (seq_segment)

title: Genomic Data: Wrappers, Hi-C, and File Connections
text: Multi-sample CN heatmap one row per sample tiles coloured CN state. rows four simulated scenarios, covering different chromosomes: chr2 amplicon (bfb), chr1-3 genome doubling (wgd), chromothripsis chr3 (ct) chromothripsis amplification chr4 (ct_bfb). One window per chromosome puts every scenario shared chr1-chr4 layout, row tiles scenario segments.
code: cnh_gr <- do.call(c, unname(Map(function(s, nm) {   GRanges(s$chrom, IRanges(s$start, s$end), sample = nm, cn = s$cn) }, segs, names(segs)))) #> Warning in .merge_two_Seqinfo_objects(x, y): The 2 combined objects have no sequence levels in common. (Use #>   suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning.)  win_hm <- GRanges(paste0("chr", 1:4),                   IRanges(1, c(248956422, 242193529, 198295559, 190214555)))  p <- seq_cn_heatmap(cnh_gr, windows = win_hm,                     sample_col = "sample", cn_col = "cn",                     sample_order = names(segs)) p$plot()

title: Genomic Data: Wrappers, Hi-C, and File Connections
text: ChIP-style signal peak tracks. data named list GRanges (one per sample) single GRanges sample column.
code: make_sig <- function(nm) {   g <- GRanges("chr1",                IRanges(sort(sample(1:1e6, 400)), width = 500),                score = rexp(400, rate = 0.15))   S4Vectors::mcols(g)$sample <- nm   g } sig <- list(Rad21 = make_sig("Rad21"), NippedB = make_sig("NippedB")) peaks <- list(Rad21   = GRanges("chr1", IRanges(sort(sample(1:1e6, 20)), width = 2000)),               NippedB = GRanges("chr1", IRanges(sort(sample(1:1e6, 15)), width = 2000)))  p <- seq_chip(sig, peaks = peaks,               windows = GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 1e6))) p$plot()

title: Genomic Data: Wrappers, Hi-C, and File Connections
text: seq_hic() renders contact matrices four styles. call produces one seq_plot single track; combine styles regions calling several times composing seq_resolve().

title: Genomic Data: Wrappers, Hi-C, and File Connections
text: simple contact simulator: every upper-triangular bin pair (, j) gets strength exp(-distance * decay_rate) * lognormal(noise), mirrored (j, ).
code: # contact simulator generate_hic_matrix <- function(n_bins, decay_rate = 0.2) {   ij    <- expand.grid(i = seq_len(n_bins), j = seq_len(n_bins))   upper <- ij$j >= ij$i   ij    <- ij[upper, , drop = FALSE]   d     <- ij$j - ij$i   s     <- pmax(0.01, exp(-d * decay_rate) * rlnorm(nrow(ij), 0, 0.3))   upper_df <- data.frame(bin_i = ij$i, bin_j = ij$j, strength = s)   off      <- d > 0   lower_df <- data.frame(bin_i = ij$j[off], bin_j = ij$i[off],                          strength = s[off])   rbind(upper_df, lower_df) }  # seq_hic-shaped GRanges for a single region hic_region <- function(chrom, start, end, bin_size, decay = 0.2,                        seed = NULL) {   if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)   bin_starts <- seq(start, end - bin_size, by = bin_size)   n          <- length(bin_starts)   mat        <- generate_hic_matrix(n, decay_rate = decay)   GRanges(chrom,           IRanges(bin_starts[mat$bin_i], width = bin_size),           i_start = bin_starts[mat$bin_i],           i_end   = bin_starts[mat$bin_i] + bin_size,           j_start = bin_starts[mat$bin_j],           j_end   = bin_starts[mat$bin_j] + bin_size,           score   = mat$strength) }  # Multi-region: per-chromosome intra-chrom matrices, concatenated. hic_multi <- function(regions, bin_size, decay = 0.2, base_seed = 100) {   parts <- lapply(seq_along(regions), function(k) {     r <- regions[[k]]     hic_region(r[[1]], r[[2]], r[[3]], bin_size,                decay = decay, seed = base_seed + k)   })   suppressWarnings(do.call(c, parts)) }

code: # x: chr1 (1 region). y: stacked chrA + chrB (2 regions). # Mixed contact set: chr1×chr1 (intra), chr1↔chrA, chr1↔chrB. set.seed(7) n_per <- 250 i_st  <- sort(sample(seq(1, 4e6 - 1e5, by = 1e5), n_per, replace = TRUE)) mk <- function(j_chrom) data.frame(   i_chrom = "chr1",   i_start = i_st, i_end = i_st + 1e5,   j_chrom = j_chrom,   j_start = sort(sample(seq(1, 4e6 - 1e5, by = 1e5), n_per, replace = TRUE)),   score   = rexp(n_per, rate = 0.4),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) df <- rbind(mk("chrA"), mk("chrB")) df$j_end <- df$j_start + 1e5  gr_multiy <- GRanges(   df$i_chrom, IRanges(df$i_start, df$i_end),   i_start = df$i_start, i_end = df$i_end,   j_chrom = df$j_chrom, j_start = df$j_start, j_end = df$j_end,   score   = df$score )  win_x_one <- GRanges("chr1",            IRanges(1, 4e6)) win_y_two <- GRanges(c("chrA", "chrB"), IRanges(c(1, 1), c(4e6, 4e6))) seq_hic(gr_multiy,         windows   = win_x_one,         y_windows = win_y_two,         style     = "full")$plot()

title: Genomic Data: Wrappers, Hi-C, and File Connections
text: combine_windows = TRUE concatenates x regions one virtual panel cross-window contacts (example translocation) appear single view. implemented seq_track() level, every track type supports . combine_y_windows y.
code: # Two-region data: intra-chr14, intra-chr5, plus a "translocation" # band of inter-chromosomal contacts concentrated near a breakpoint. set.seed(11) bs   <- 1e5  # bin size mk_intra <- function(chrom, start, end, decay = 0.25, seed_off = 0) {   starts <- seq(start, end - bs, by = bs)   n      <- length(starts)   set.seed(seed_off)   mat <- generate_hic_matrix(n, decay_rate = decay)   data.frame(i_chrom = chrom,  i_start = starts[mat$bin_i],              i_end   = starts[mat$bin_i] + bs,              j_chrom = chrom,  j_start = starts[mat$bin_j],              j_end   = starts[mat$bin_j] + bs,              score   = mat$strength,              stringsAsFactors = FALSE) } mk_inter <- function(c1, s1, e1, c2, s2, e2, n = 200, focus = c(0.4, 0.7)) {   i_st <- s1 + round(runif(n, focus[1], focus[2]) * (e1 - s1) / bs) * bs   j_st <- s2 + round(runif(n, focus[1], focus[2]) * (e2 - s2) / bs) * bs   rbind(     data.frame(i_chrom = c1, i_start = i_st, i_end = i_st + bs,                j_chrom = c2, j_start = j_st, j_end = j_st + bs,                score   = rexp(n, rate = 0.4) + 0.5,                stringsAsFactors = FALSE),     data.frame(i_chrom = c2, i_start = j_st, i_end = j_st + bs,                j_chrom = c1, j_start = i_st, j_end = i_st + bs,                score   = rexp(n, rate = 0.4) + 0.5,                stringsAsFactors = FALSE)   ) }  intra14 <- mk_intra("chr14", 98e6,  100e6, seed_off = 1) intra5  <- mk_intra("chr5",  170e6, 172e6, seed_off = 2) inter   <- mk_inter("chr14", 98e6,  100e6, "chr5", 170e6, 172e6, n = 250) all_df  <- rbind(intra14, intra5, inter)  gr_combined <- GRanges(   all_df$i_chrom, IRanges(all_df$i_start, all_df$i_end),   i_start = all_df$i_start, i_end = all_df$i_end,   j_chrom = all_df$j_chrom, j_start = all_df$j_start, j_end = all_df$j_end,   score   = all_df$score ) win_combined <- GRanges(c("chr14", "chr5"),                         IRanges(c(98e6, 170e6), c(100e6, 172e6))) seq_hic(gr_combined,         windows         = win_combined,         style           = "triangle",         combine_windows = TRUE,         palette         = "reds")$plot() seq_hic(gr_combined,         windows           = win_combined,         y_windows         = win_combined,         style             = "full",         combine_windows   = TRUE,         combine_y_windows = TRUE,         palette           = "reds")$plot()

title: Layouts: Windows, Margins, Sizing, and Patchwork
text: Every track allocated rectangular cell page layout partitioned five nested zones, two track level three window level: Track outer margin — outermost band track cell. Axis titles (taken track mapping) drawn . seq_track(track_outer_margin = ...). Default 0.02. Track inner margin — separates title band window row. seq_track(track_inner_margin = ...). Default 0.02. Window outer margin — per-window spacer inside track plot region. seq_track(window_outer_margin = ...). Default 0. Window inner margin — per-window band holding axis lines, ticks, tick labels. seq_track(window_inner_margin = ...). Default 0.02. Plot area — remains per window. Elements render ; panel$inner carries coordinates. Axis lines sit boundary plot area window inner margin. gap adjacent windows plot- track-level aes("window.gap.width" = ...) (default 0.01); gap tracks plot-level trackGaps (default 0.01). old seq_track(window_margin = ...) constructor argument deprecated — see Window gap width . schematic lays two tracks × two windows using nothing SeqPlotR, zone coloured via plot-level trackBackground, trackInnerBackground, windowBoxBackground, windowInnerBackground, windowBackground aesthetics. seq_text places label plot area.  Reading schematic, outside inside track: Pink — track outer margin (axis titles live ). Yellow — track inner margin. Purple — window outer margin (per-window spacer). Green — window inner margin (axis lines, ticks, tick labels live ). Blue — plot area, elements render. vertical green/blue split inside track window margin two windows. horizontal gap two tracks track gap.
code: # Two windows (2 Mb and 1.5 Mb wide). schematic_win <- GRanges(   "chr1", IRanges(start = c(1e6, 5e6), end = c(3e6, 6.5e6)))  # One label centred inside each window for each track. mk_labels <- function(track_name) {   GRanges(     "chr1", IRanges(start = c(2e6, 5.75e6), width = 1),     label = paste0(track_name, "\nWindow ", c(1, 2))   ) } lbl_A <- mk_labels("Track A") lbl_B <- mk_labels("Track B")  # Zone colors via plot-level aesthetics; axes turned off so the five # nested rectangles are visible without interference. schematic_aes <- aes(   trackBackground        = "#F89A8A",  # track outer margin   trackBorder            = "grey30",   trackInnerBackground   = "#ECCB60",  # track inner margin   trackInnerBorder       = "grey30",   windowBoxBackground    = "#A699D0",  # window outer margin   windowBoxBorder        = "grey30",   windowInnerBackground  = "#BEC97E",  # window inner margin   windowInnerBorder      = "grey30",   windowBackground       = "#92BFDB",  # plot area   windowBorder           = "grey30",   xAxisLine = FALSE, xAxisTicks = FALSE, xAxisLabels = FALSE,   xAxisTitle = FALSE,   yAxisLine = FALSE, yAxisTicks = FALSE, yAxisLabels = FALSE,   yAxisTitle = FALSE,   trackGaps = 0.04,   "window.gap.width" = 0.03 )  seq_plot(aesthetics = schematic_aes) %|%   seq_track(track_id = "A",             data = lbl_A,             mapping = map(x = start, label = label),             windows = schematic_win,             track_outer_margin  = 0.035,             track_inner_margin  = 0.025,             window_outer_margin = 0.025,             window_inner_margin = 0.035) %+%   seq_text(aesthetics = aes(fontsize = 12, color = "#1C1B1A")) %__%   seq_track(track_id = "B",             data = lbl_B,             mapping = map(x = start, label = label),             windows = schematic_win,             track_outer_margin  = 0.035,             track_inner_margin  = 0.025,             window_outer_margin = 0.025,             window_inner_margin = 0.035) %+%   seq_text(aesthetics = aes(fontsize = 12, color = "#1C1B1A")) -> p p$plot()

title: Layouts: Windows, Margins, Sizing, and Patchwork
text: aes("window.gap.width" = <npc>) controls horizontal gap adjacent windows within track. Set seq_plot() apply across every track, specific seq_track() override plot-level value track . Default 0.01.  legacy seq_track(window_margin = ...) constructor argument deprecated emits warning used; switch aes("window.gap.width" = ...). older aes(window_gaps = ...) key still works alias window.gap.width takes priority set.
code: gap_win <- GRanges(   "chr1",   IRanges(start = c(1, 1e6 + 1, 2e6 + 1), width = 1e6) ) gap_lbl <- function(track_name) {   GRanges(     "chr1",     IRanges(start = c(5e5, 1.5e6, 2.5e6), width = 1),     label = paste0(track_name, "\nW", c(1, 2, 3))   ) }  # Three tracks, three gap widths: collapsed, default, generous. seq_plot(aesthetics = aes(     windowBackground = "#92BFDB", windowBorder = "grey30",     xAxisLine = FALSE, xAxisTicks = FALSE, xAxisLabels = FALSE,     xAxisTitle = FALSE, yAxisLine = FALSE, yAxisTicks = FALSE,     yAxisLabels = FALSE, yAxisTitle = FALSE,     "window.gap.width" = 0   # plot-level default for all tracks   )) %|%   seq_track(track_id = "Collapsed (0)",             data = gap_lbl("Collapsed"),             mapping = map(x = start, label = label),             windows = gap_win) %+%   seq_text(aesthetics = aes(fontsize = 11)) %__%   seq_track(track_id = "Default (0.01)",             data = gap_lbl("Default"),             mapping = map(x = start, label = label),             windows = gap_win,             aesthetics = aes("window.gap.width" = 0.01)) %+%   seq_text(aesthetics = aes(fontsize = 11)) %__%   seq_track(track_id = "Generous (0.05)",             data = gap_lbl("Generous"),             mapping = map(x = start, label = label),             windows = gap_win,             aesthetics = aes("window.gap.width" = 0.05)) %+%   seq_text(aesthetics = aes(fontsize = 11)) -> p p$plot()

title: Layouts: Windows, Margins, Sizing, and Patchwork
text: Relative sizing controlled three arguments: track_width (within row), track_height (across rows), scale mcols column windows GRanges (within track’s plot region). Unequal track widths one row. Track 3× wider B.  Unequal track heights stacked rows. points track twice tall bar track .  Per-window scale factor. Within multi-window track, windows sized width(windows) * mcols(windows)$scale. Defaults auto-inferred scale windows. Setting one window’s scale 0 shrinks nothing; setting distinct scales compresses expands individual windows relative others.  Track-level unit override window_scale. 3):min(n, pk + 3)     scores[w] <- scores[w] + runif(length(w), 0.4, 0.85)   }   GRanges("chr1", IRanges(starts, width = 1), score = pmin(scores, 1)) } gr_a <- make_chip(seed = 1) gr_b <- make_chip(seed = 2)  # continuous scores for gradient examples set.seed(42) gr_cnt <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(sort(sample(1:999000, 120)), width = 1),                   score = round(runif(120, 0, 100), 1))  # contact-map-like tiles n_bins <- 60 starts_hic <- seq(1, 1e6, length.out = n_bins + 1)[-(n_bins + 1)] pairs <- expand.grid(i = seq_len(n_bins), j = seq_len(n_bins)) pairs <- pairs[pairs$j >= pairs$i, ] gr_tiles <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(starts_hic[pairs$i], width = 1e6 / n_bins),                     y = pairs$j,                     fill = pmax(0, pmin(1, round(exp(-(pairs$j - pairs$i) * 0.08) +                                                    rnorm(nrow(pairs), 0, 0.05), 3))))  # simulated chromothripsis on chr3: somatic SNVs and copy-number segments sim <- function(f) utils::read.delim(system.file("extdata", "sim", "ct", f, package = "SeqPlotR")) snv <- sim("snvs.tsv") snv <- GRanges(snv$chrom, IRanges(snv$pos, width = 1), vaf = snv$vaf, depth = snv$depth,                sbs6 = snv$sbs6, clonality = ifelse(snv$clonal, "clonal", "subclonal")) seg <- sim("segments.tsv") seg <- GRanges(seg$chrom, IRanges(seg$start, seg$end), cn = seg$cn,                state = ifelse(seg$cn > 2, "gain", ifelse(seg$cn < 2, "loss", "neutral"))) win_ct <- GRanges("chr3", IRanges(9.5e7, 1.95e8))  # right margin wide enough for auto-generated legends right_margin <- aes(margins = list(top = 0, right = 0.25, bottom = 0, left = 0))

title: Legends
text: Mapping column color, fill shape generates legend seq_legend() call. Discrete columns give keyed legend (flexoki palette; shapes cycle circle, square, triangle, diamond) numeric columns give viridis color bar. Auto-legends go right track margin, reserve space plot-level margins aesthetic. explicit legend always overrides auto-generation. examples use simulated chromothripsis sample. snv holds somatic SNVs chr3 (variant allele fraction, read depth, six-class mutation type sbs6, whether SNV clonal), seg holds copy-number segments, shattered region 100 190 Mb oscillates copy number 3 1. Mapping color mutation type gives six-level discrete legend: Six-level discrete color legend SNV mutation type right track margin. Mapping shape clonality marks clonal subclonal SNVs different glyphs: Shape legend auto-generated map(shape = clonality) right track margin. numeric column gives color bar. read depth y axis, drops copy number falls 1, color shows variant allele fraction: Viridis color bar auto tick axis SNV variant allele fraction. applies elements, including seq_bar, seq_segment seq_tile heatmaps. Copy-number segments drawn bars take fill gain, loss neutral state: Copy-number segment bars discrete fill legend map(fill = state). seq_segment draws one horizontal line per copy-number segment, colored state: seq_segment discrete color legend map(color = state). numeric fill gives gradient. bar fill follows integer copy number: Copy-number segment bars continuous fill gradient map(fill = cn). tile heatmap keeps contact-map tiles, since simulated data contact matrix: Contact-map tiles auto gradient legend.

code: bfb_seg <- sim("ct_bfb", "segments") bfb_seg <- bfb_seg[bfb_seg$end > 5.8e7 & bfb_seg$start < 1.24e8, ] seg_gr  <- GRanges(bfb_seg$chrom, IRanges(bfb_seg$start, bfb_seg$end),                    cn = bfb_seg$cn)  snv <- sim("ct_bfb", "snvs") snv <- snv[snv$pos > 5.8e7 & snv$pos < 1.24e8, ] snv_gr <- GRanges(snv$chrom, IRanges(snv$pos, width = 1), vaf = snv$vaf)  bfb_sv$cn0  <- 1 bfb_sv$vaf1 <- 0.8 seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(track_id = "CN", windows = bfb_win, track_height = 1.2) %+%     seq_segment(data = seg_gr,                 mapping = map(x = start, x_end = end, y = cn, y_end = cn),                 aesthetics = aes(color = "#205EA6", linewidth = 2)) %__%   seq_track(track_id = "SNV", windows = bfb_win, track_height = 1.2) %+%     seq_point(data = snv_gr, mapping = map(x = start, y = vaf),               aesthetics = aes(color = "#66800B", size = 0.25,                                alpha = 0.5)) %+%   seq_string(data = bfb_sv,              map(x0 = pos1, x1 = pos2, chrom0 = chrom1, chrom1 = chrom2,                  strand0 = strand1, strand1 = strand2,                  y0 = cn0, y1 = vaf1),              t0 = "CN", t1 = "SNV",              aesthetics = aes(color = "#AF3029", linewidth = 1.1,                               alpha = 0.75)) -> p p$plot()

code: # Overview spans 5 Mb; detail zooms into 1.6 – 2.4 Mb. overview_win <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1,      5e6)) detail_win   <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1.6e6,  2.4e6))  xs_o  <- seq(1,      5e6,   length.out = 160) xs_d  <- seq(1.6e6,  2.4e6, length.out = 120) sig_o <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(xs_o, width = 1),                  score = 0.5 + 0.3 * sin((xs_o - 1) / 6e5)) sig_d <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(xs_d, width = 1),                  score = 0.5 + 0.3 * sin((xs_d - 1) / 6e5) +                          rnorm(length(xs_d), 0, 0.03))  zoom_region <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1.6e6, 2.4e6))  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(track_id = "Overview", windows = overview_win,             track_height = 0.5) %+%     seq_area(data = sig_o, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),              aesthetics = aes(fill = "#4385BE", alpha = 0.55)) %__%   seq_track(track_id = "Detail", windows = detail_win,             track_height = 1.3) %+%     seq_area(data = sig_d, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),              aesthetics = aes(fill = "#205EA6", alpha = 0.8)) %+%   seq_zoom(data = zoom_region,            map(x0 = start, x0_end = end),            t0 = "Overview", t1 = "Detail",            aesthetics = aes(fill = "#878580", alpha = 0.2,                             color = "#878580", linewidth = 0.4)) -> p p$plot()

Drop wide overview top row pair two independent detail panels , emit one seq_zoom per detail region. plot-level links validate t0 t1 refer tracks already added plot, zooms go end chain.   zoom polygon inherits color destination track, left right fan-outs visually distinguishable glance. idiom scales panels — add letters layout string’s second row matching seq_zoom per region.
code: fan_layout <- " AAAA BBCC " seq_preview_layout(layout = fan_layout) # Overview spans chr1:1-5 Mb; B zooms into 1.2-1.8 Mb, C into 3.2-4.0 Mb. overview_win <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1,      5e6)) detail_b_win <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1.2e6,  1.8e6)) detail_c_win <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(3.2e6,  4.0e6))  xs_a  <- seq(1,      5e6,   length.out = 200) xs_b  <- seq(1.2e6,  1.8e6, length.out =  80) xs_c  <- seq(3.2e6,  4.0e6, length.out =  80) mk_sig <- function(xs, jitter = 0) {   GRanges("chr1", IRanges(xs, width = 1),           score = 0.5 + 0.3 * sin((xs - 1) / 5e5) +                   rnorm(length(xs), 0, jitter)) } sig_a <- mk_sig(xs_a, jitter = 0.00) sig_b <- mk_sig(xs_b, jitter = 0.03) sig_c <- mk_sig(xs_c, jitter = 0.03)  zoom_b <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1.2e6, 1.8e6)) zoom_c <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(3.2e6, 4.0e6))  seq_plot(layout = fan_layout) %+%   seq_track(track_id = "A", windows = overview_win) %+%     seq_area(data = sig_a, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),              aesthetics = aes(fill = "#4385BE", alpha = 0.55)) %+%   seq_track(track_id = "B", windows = detail_b_win) %+%     seq_area(data = sig_b, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),              aesthetics = aes(fill = "#66800B", alpha = 0.8)) %+%   seq_track(track_id = "C", windows = detail_c_win) %+%     seq_area(data = sig_c, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),              aesthetics = aes(fill = "#AF3029", alpha = 0.8)) %+%   seq_zoom(data = zoom_b, map(x0 = start, x0_end = end),            t0 = "A", t1 = "B",            aesthetics = aes(fill = "#66800B", alpha = 0.22,                             color = "#66800B", linewidth = 0.5)) %+%   seq_zoom(data = zoom_c, map(x0 = start, x0_end = end),            t0 = "A", t1 = "C",            aesthetics = aes(fill = "#AF3029", alpha = 0.22,                             color = "#AF3029", linewidth = 0.5)) -> p p$plot()

code: win <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 1e6)) xs  <- seq(1, 1e6, length.out = 400) mk_sig <- function(seed, freq, jitter = 0.03) {   set.seed(seed)   GRanges("chr1", IRanges(xs, width = 1),           score = 0.5 + 0.3 * sin((xs - 1) / freq) +                   rnorm(length(xs), 0, jitter)) } sig_a <- mk_sig(1, 1.5e5) sig_b <- mk_sig(2, 2.0e5) sig_c <- mk_sig(3, 2.5e5)  # Two genomic regions to flag across all three tracks. hl <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(2.0e5, 6.5e5),                               c(2.6e5, 7.4e5)))  seq_plot() %|%   seq_track(track_id = "A", windows = win) %+%     seq_area(data = sig_a, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),              aesthetics = aes(fill = "#4385BE", alpha = 0.7)) %__%   seq_track(track_id = "B", windows = win) %+%     seq_area(data = sig_b, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),              aesthetics = aes(fill = "#205EA6", alpha = 0.7)) %__%   seq_track(track_id = "C", windows = win) %+%     seq_area(data = sig_c, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),              aesthetics = aes(fill = "#24837B", alpha = 0.7)) %+%   seq_highlight(data = hl, map(x0 = start, x0_end = end),                 t0 = "A", t1 = "C",                 aesthetics = aes(fill = "#AF3029", alpha = 0.18)) -> p p$plot()

title: Timing: Event-Time Elements and the ROSE Adapter
text: seq_scale_count(max, log) builds copy-number axis integer ticks. log = TRUE uses pseudo-log transform (values 1 stay linear, larger values placed 1 + log2(v)) labels ticks 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Every element track, including seq_point seq_arch, receives transform, values given count units. seq_paired_ribbon() draws two thin ribbons per span: y_up upward y_down downward.
code: bands <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(1, 4e5), c(4e5, 1e6)), major = c(2, 12), minor = c(1, 4)) snv <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(1e5, 5e5, 8e5), width = 1), m = c(1.1, 11, 6))  seq_plot(aesthetics = page) %+%   seq_track(     track_id = "cn", windows = win,     scale_y = seq_scale_count(12, log = TRUE),     aesthetics = aes("axis.y.title.text" = "Copy number (log scale)"),     elements = list(       seq_paired_ribbon(bands, map(y_up = major, y_down = minor),                         legend_labels = c(up = "Major CN", down = "Minor CN")),       seq_point(snv, map(y = m))     )   ) -> p p$plot()

text: %|% %__% kept shorthand alternatives reduce verbosity common cases: strictly aliases — logic lives %+%. Using %|% %__% non-SeqTrack RHS falls %+% dispatch.
code: `%|%`  <- function(e1, e2) e1 %+% (if (inherits(e2, "SeqTrack")) { e2$direction <- "right"; e2 } else e2) `%__%` <- function(e1, e2) e1 %+% (if (inherits(e2, "SeqTrack")) { e2$direction <- "under"; e2 } else e2) # These are equivalent: seq_plot() %+% seq_track(direction="right") %+% seq_point() %+% seq_track(direction="under") seq_plot() %|% seq_track() %+% seq_point() %__% seq_track() seq_plot() %+%   seq_track(track_id = "Signal", direction = "right", windows = win) %+% seq_area(map(x=start, y=score)) %+%   seq_track(track_id = "CN",     direction = "right", windows = win) %+% seq_point(map(x=start, y=logR))  %+%   seq_track(track_id = "Genes",  direction = "under", windows = win) %+% seq_gene(map(x=start, type=type, strand=strand)) %+%   seq_string(data=links, map(x=start, y=score), data2=links, mapping2=map(x=end, y=score), t0="Signal", t1="CN") %+%   seq_annotation() # Row 1: Signal | CN # Row 2: Genes # Plot-level: string link + annotation (deferred, drawn last)

title: Genomic Visualization with a Layered Grammar
text: Captures unevaluated R expressions. prep() time, expression evaluated mcols(data) evaluation environment calling frame enclosing environment: Specials (start, end, width, mid) injected directly evaluation environment alongside mcols columns. means bare symbols (map(x = start)) compound expressions (map(x = (start + end) / 2)) resolve correctly single eval() call without branching.
code: map <- function(...) structure(as.list(substitute(list(...)))[-1], class = "SeqMap") .resolve_mapping <- function(data, mapping, env = parent.frame()) {   if (is.null(data) || is.null(mapping)) return(list())   specials <- list(     start = BiocGenerics::start(data),     end   = BiocGenerics::end(data),     width = BiocGenerics::width(data),     mid   = (BiocGenerics::start(data) + BiocGenerics::end(data)) / 2   )   # Inject specials into the eval environment alongside mcols so that both   # bare symbols (map(x = start)) and compound expressions (map(x = (start+end)/2))   # resolve correctly without separate branching.   eval_env <- c(specials, as.list(S4Vectors::mcols(data)))   lapply(mapping, function(expr) eval(expr, envir = eval_env, enclos = env)) }

what: aes() — constant aesthetics and theme keys
title: Genomic Visualization with a Layered Grammar
text: Captures evaluated values. Used two purposes: 1. Element aesthetics — static visual properties: aes(color="blue", linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.8) 2. Theme/axis keys — hierarchical dotted-key namespace controlling track chrome axis appearance. Two equivalent forms accepted: Theme key inheritance: keys follow 3-level hierarchy. missing specific key falls back less-specific parent: - axis.x1.line.col → axis.x.line.col → axis.line.col Hard break legacy names: old flat aesthetic names (xAxisLine, axisColor, trackBackground, etc.) longer accepted. theme control uses dotted-key namespace.
code: aes <- function(...) structure(list(...), class = "SeqAes") # Flat dotted-key form aes(axis.x.line.col = "red", track.background.fill = "white")  # Nested form (flattened automatically) aes(axis.x = aes(line = aes(col = "red")), track = aes(background = aes(fill = "white")))

Build a nrow x ncol character matrix   # 4. For each unique non-'#' letter:   #    - Find all (row, col) positions   #    - Compute min_row, max_row, min_col, max_col   #    - Verify every cell in that bounding box is the same letter (error if not — non-rectangular regions are invalid)   #    - Store as list: letter -> list(r0, r1, c0, c1)   # 5. Return: list(matrix = m, regions = regions, nrow = nrow, ncol = ncol) } x0 = (c0 - 1) / ncol;  x1 = c1 / ncol y0 = 1 - r1 / nrow;    y1 = 1 - (r0 - 1) / nrow   # y is top-to-bottom in the string
